clue.text: Take a photograph of monster flower

parts.note: to snap is to take a quick photograph
a dragon is a fire-breathing monster of legend

explanation.surface: An instruction to photograph some monstrous bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant grown for its colourful blooms.

clue.text: A quarter had the fish

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters or cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone ate a quarter portion of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A compass point is one of the four quarters, so 'A quarter' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like sea fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: A piece intended to be voiced flat

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: a part (a piece) plus meant (intended)

explanation.surface: A musical piece meant to be sung in a flattened key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece intended' is A PART MEANT; said out loud it sounds like the answer. 'Flat' suggests music but is a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is the British word for a set of rooms on one floor, which Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Crowded together, which is stupid

explanation.surface: Something both crowded and dim-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick covers both senses: things packed tightly, and a person slow to understand.

clue.text: A whacking to sicken a woman

parts.note: whacking means huge, as in a whacking great bill
to ail is to fall ill or feel unwell

explanation.surface: A beating that leaves someone feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A whacking' looks like a beating; here whacking is an adjective meaning very large.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, and in older English also a lady's maid.

clue.text: Noel put out? That's rich!

indicators.note: put out suggests annoyed, but out here signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone notices Noel is upset and remarks that this is a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the seven letters of NOEL PUT; 'That's rich!' sounds like an exclamation but its last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy or luxurious.

clue.text: No longer writing about the Church

parts.note: a book on birds is writing about birds, so on stands for about here
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped writing about religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some earlier time but not now.

clue.text: Set on returning the money

indicators.note: in this down clue returning means the letters of set on are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to get their cash back.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper money.

clue.text: Finish up very annoyed when compromised

parts.note: to end is to finish up
angered means made very annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone ends up furious after a deal goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put at risk, as an endangered species is threatened with extinction.

clue.text: He daren't upset a fan

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the words before it are spilled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is afraid of offending one of his supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the eight letters of HE DARENT (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or person.

clue.text: Showing a profit, not for the first time

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Showing a profit once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more, a repeat occurrence.

clue.text: At home, having no engagement, so soaked

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
undated, with no date booked, means having no social engagement

explanation.surface: Someone stays home with nothing in the diary and ends up drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests marriage; here it is a date, so having none is UNDATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded or drenched, overwhelmed with water.

clue.text: See great changes in the lowest class

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words before it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Observing great social shifts among the poorest people.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest accommodation on a passenger ship was the bottom grade of travel.

clue.text: The city where one has to eat German-style

explanation.surface: A town where everyone dines the German way.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Germany's Ruhr, and also the German verb meaning to dine.

clue.text: Reading about medical back-up being critical

indicators.note: about says the reading word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully

indicators.note: in this down clue back-up means the abbreviation for medical is read upwards, in reverse

explanation.surface: A study of medical reserves that finds fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the act of reading aloud; it stands for the old verb to con, study. In a down clue 'back-up' means the medical abbreviation reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemning means passing harsh judgment, denouncing.

clue.text: Superior with everybody in general

parts.note: over means above or superior to
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Someone ranked above everyone in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means taken as a whole, on balance.

clue.text: Sent a tie maybe, or something to drink

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the words before it could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A gift choice: a tie or a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur flavoured with aniseed.

clue.text: Even the most restless can offer some support

indicators.note: offering some of a phrase means part of its letters, here running across two words

explanation.surface: Even the most fidgety person can be supportive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs that holds up a tabletop.

clue.text: Got to be dismissed!

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means proved or became, and also expelled or thrown out.

clue.text: Holds back stained material

indicators.note: material as a stuff to be worked up signals that the letters of stained are reworked

explanation.surface: Fabric with marks on it keeps someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like cloth to go with 'stained', but it rearranges STAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to keep someone from leaving, restrain them.

clue.text: Boy taking in press operator

indicators.note: taking in says the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a son is a boy
to urge is to press someone

explanation.surface: A lad taking a job working a printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' suggests machinery; it is someone who carries out operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical specialist who performs operations.

clue.text: Released a certain party without charging

parts.note: a set is a particular group or party of people
free means at no charge

explanation.surface: A group let off without being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charging' suggests police charges, but it means asking payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone, let them go.

clue.text: Tense period of confinement

explanation.surface: An anxious time spent locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten or pull taut, and slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Doctor with practice-a little beast

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
use means habit or practice

explanation.surface: A doctor's surgery has a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent, a little creature.

clue.text: A French writer makes free

parts.note: un is French for a
a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: A French author liberates someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpen is to release an animal from an enclosure.

clue.text: Diverted by the regal lady, striking in red

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces go inside the word for red

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
workers who are striking are out

explanation.surface: Sent another way by a queen hitting someone in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests hitting, but workers on strike are out. 'The regal lady' is the Queen's cipher, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent by another route, as traffic is redirected.

clue.text: Some proud Derbyshire farmer supplying milk

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A proud dairy farmer from Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The cow's milk-giving gland, cryptically called the farmer's milk supply.

clue.text: The guy calling for beer-cold

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A man shouting for a chilled pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, as in a smart one who knows it all.

clue.text: Inapt time maybe to get snappy

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the words before it might be put in another order

explanation.surface: A bad moment to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and short-tempered, quick to snap at people.

clue.text: Making old coppers turn funny

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for pence in pre-decimal British money
a roll is a turn over

explanation.surface: Seeing old policemen turn is amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; it is copper coins, and D stood for old British pennies before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Wryly amusing, quietly humorous.

clue.text: Scots go for this band

explanation.surface: A Scottish band goes for it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect to gang is to walk or go; also a group of people.

clue.text: Solitary job of work in bizarre situation

indicators.note: in says the job goes inside the bizarre word

parts.note: antic means grotesque or bizarre
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A lonely task in a strange setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a hermit or recluse living apart from the world.
